goal: Check whether people who work out at home or at the gym share two problems: (A) losing count or skipping sets because of distraction, and (B) planning workouts in a notebook or notes being slow and hard to change. Informs hypotheses HA0-HA6 and HB1-HB4 in documentation/hipotezy-produktowe.md. Note: in this study 'app_type' is a group of exercisers and 'app_name' is a community or topic, not an app.

app_types.label: people working out at home (home gym, bodyweight, small equipment)
people lifting at a commercial gym
beginners and casual exercisers building a routine
how people track and plan workouts: notebook, notes, spreadsheet, app

categories.name: Losing Count/Reps
categories.use_for: forgetting how many reps or sets were done within a set or exercise, losing the count mid-set

categories.name: Skipped Sets/Exercises
categories.use_for: accidentally skipping a set or an exercise, realizing afterwards that part of the plan was not done

categories.name: Lost Place After Break
categories.use_for: not knowing where one is after a rest, a pause, a phone call, or switching away

categories.name: Distraction/Interruptions
categories.use_for: being talked to, mind wandering, or distracted by people or noise during the workout

categories.name: Rest Timing
categories.use_for: tracking rest between sets, resting too long or too short, timers

categories.name: Planning Effort
categories.use_for: planning workouts takes too much time or effort, building a program from scratch

categories.name: Plan Changes/Editing
categories.use_for: changing a plan is hard or messy, crossing out, rewriting, adjusting weights or exercises

categories.name: Reuse/Templates
categories.use_for: rewriting the same plan again, copying previous weeks, wanting templates or repeatable routines

categories.name: Paper vs App
categories.use_for: comparisons or trade-offs between a notebook, notes, a spreadsheet and an app

categories.name: Progress Tracking
categories.use_for: remembering last weights, seeing progress, reviewing history

categories.name: Phone During Workout
categories.use_for: using or avoiding the phone during training, screen locking, phone as a distraction

categories.name: Coping Workarounds
categories.use_for: tricks people use to avoid losing track, such as counting aloud, marking sets, writing on hand

categories.name: Motivation/Consistency
categories.use_for: staying motivated, sticking to a routine, skipping whole workouts

categories.name: Other
categories.use_for: anything that does not fit above

severity.high: the problem recurs and hurts the workout, or makes the person abandon their method

rules.duplicates: one row per opinion; drop only exact duplicates
rules.store_review_url: app store or aggregator page when the review has no own link
rules.inferred_dates: keep (decided 2026-10-18): dates inferred from 'N months ago' or item ids are kept when inside the range; mark them in the run note
rules.developer_posts: keep (decided 2026-10-18): first-person anecdotes by app builders or authors who sell tools are kept; mark them in the run note
rules.weak_fit_rows: keep (decided 2026-10-18): rows flagged as weak fits stay, with low severity and category Motivation/Consistency or Other

runs.note: Exa 4 types + Reddit two passes (second targeted). Kept per user: 9 HN rows with inferred dates, developer/seller posts, weak-fit rows. Reddit gave mostly noise; problem B has no Reddit voices.
